VER, 26.1

Regulations League Structure

provisions.title: Leagues
provisions.body:
There are three (3) leagues

● Buhurt (Group Fight)
● Duels
● Outrance/Profights

provisions.title: Regions
provisions.body:
Each country is its own Region. If a country has less than 15 members, it is asked that they join another nearby country or countries to form a Region. This will help smaller countries be competitive. If countries wish to make a Region, they can do so for a season at a time.
With approval from the BI Council. Each case will be looked at separately.

provisions.title: Divisions
provisions.body:
Divisions will be based on National Org discretion for the 2026 season. We will use the standings to establish an appropriate standard in the future. There will be the option for Regions to divide into Divisions :

● Division 1 (for each Men’s Category) : Top Tier Teams and Duellist’s will be put into Division 1. National Organisations will Promote or Demote Teams and Duelist’s with the Buhurt International Committee confirming.

● Division 2 (for each Men’s Category) : Lower Tier Teams and Duelist’s will be put into Division 2. National Organisations will Promote or Demote Teams and Duelist’s with the Buhurt International Committee confirming.

● Division 1 (for each Women's Category) : Until enough teams and duellist’s to make 2 Divisions.

Important : This for competitive level of tournaments, to allow for newer/lower skill teams more competitive events.

provisions.title: Seasons time frame
provisions.body:
● Start: January 15th
● Ends: December 1st each year.
● Licenses: All Competitors can renew membership for the following season starting November 1st each year.

provisions.title: Ranking System
provisions.body: All points a team/duellist earns in a tournament, no matter what region the tournament was held, will go towards that team’s/duelist’s ranking.

provisions.title: Regional Rank
provisions.body: Promotes Teams/competitors to get a Regional ranking.

provisions.title: Conference Rank
provisions.body: Promotes Teams/competitors to get a Conference Ranking.

provisions.title: International Rank
provisions.body:
Promotes teams/competitors to get an International ranking.

Important : All registered BI teams have priority in event registration over unregistered Teams at Classic and above Tournaments.

provisions.title: Regional Ranking for Season
provisions.body: It is requested, Top 3 Teams and Duellist’s in each Category get trophies/medals paid for by the National Organisations.

provisions.title: Conference Ranking for Season
provisions.body: The Top Team and Duellist in each Category get a Medal/trophy paid by Buhurt International.

provisions.title: International Ranking for Invitationals
provisions.body:
Top 2 duelist(per category), top 2 groupfight teams for male and female competitors will be invited every other year to the Invitationals to be ranked as the best in World.
Invitationals are based on a 2 year season-ranking for invitationals will be based on your top 5 tournaments in a given category

provisions.title: Tournament types
provisions.body:
There are 5 Tournament Types.
Notice an Event can hold multiple types and or levels of tournaments at the same venue.

Example: "Men's 5s can be Classic, while the Women's 5s can be Source. Alternatively, you could have an Exhibition 5s and a Women's Classic Longsword tournament, all at the same event."

provisions.title: Exhibition (Buhurt/Duels)
provisions.body: Tournaments that are just for Promotion. These may not even be a Tournament. It can be a small festival where just one Club attends for fun fights. No Points given.

provisions.title: Source
provisions.body:
For developing Regions that struggle to meet the Classic criteria. Regions with developing Buhurt and Duels communities may have Source Tournaments to help promote low population areas. Established Regions may not use this without special request

All Source tournaments need to be approved by the Buhurt International Committee to make sure this level of tournament is being used correctly. And must be submitted to BI 45 days in advance

provisions.title: Clarification
provisions.body:
Regional and Conference Tournaments can be independent based on.

● League Categories (Duels or Buhurt)
● Gender Categories

For example:
"One could host a Women’s Duels Conference Tournament and a Men’s Duels Conference Tournament on different days and at different locations. Additionally, there could be a regional tournament for duels, held as a separate event from regional group fights."

Unregistered Teams made up of Licensed Members are always allowed at events. But priority must be given to Registered Teams
A men’s team may have from 5 to 20 competitors.
A women’s team may have 3 to 20 competitors.

provisions.title: A men’s team may register to a tournament from 5 to 8 competitors for 5v5
provisions.body: tournaments or 3 to 5 competitors for 3v3 tournaments.

provisions.title: A women’s team may register to a tournament from 3 to 8 competitors for a 5v5
provisions.body: tournament or 3 to 5 competitors for 3v3 tournaments
A competitor must not be on more than one team’s roster for a tournament.
A competitor must not be on more than one team’s roster for the League.

If a team is attending a tournament and wishes to field two squads at a single event, they must state which squad is earning points before the tournament begins.

Important: A team may field at multiple events and earn league points at each of those events.
No valid teams are required for the 12vs12 but only licensed competitors.

provisions.title: A team may register to a tournament from 12-20 competitors for a 12v12
provisions.body: tournament.
A competitor must not be on more than one team roster for a tournament.

provisions.title: When a 12s is formed the competitors must decide which team will collect the points
provisions.body: Important: Only the named team for that tournament will earn league points. All other clubs that form the singular team will not earn points for that event.

provisions.title: League Score are earned in the following way for Duels and Buhurt (all points are
provisions.body:
cumulative)

● 1 point for every match victory in the Pools/round robin segment of the tourney.
● 2 pts for every match victory in the brackets/elimination segment of the tourney.
● No points earned for finals except for standings (2 pts for 3rd, 4 pts for 2nd, 6 pts for 1st).

provisions.title: The multiplier for each tier
provisions.body:
● x1 for Classic
● x1.25 for Regional
● x1.5 for Conference

provisions.title: Outrance/Profight : Scoring can be found in the Outrance Regulations document
At a single Event- only one of each category may be ranked. Example - a running 2
provisions.body: longsword categories, only one of those may be ranked if containing the same competitors.

provisions.title: Season Record
provisions.body: All conferences use the top 3 tournaments average for overall standing. Highest overall score will also be acknowledged and appropriately credited.
Ranking average will use 0 for results until a team/competitor completes 3 events.

provisions.title: Dropping/no show
provisions.body:
● -5 pts for the league score for dropping from a tournament, within 72 hours of the start of the tournament.
● The category should still happen and all other competitors/teams will still be eligible for earning points and being a ranked event, as long as the category would have had the appropriate numbers

provisions.title: Mercenaries
provisions.body:
● A team that has licensed competitors on its roster at an event that are not registered on their team-profile on the official buhurt international website.
No points will be earned for that event and get status: invalid team
● Unregistered teams must be made up of Licensed Members and are always allowed at events. But get status: invalid. But priority must be given to registered teams.
● 12s may have mercenaries without penalty

Important: Women's teams must field at least 3 from their roster and can have up to 5 mercs without penalty.

provisions.title: Cards
provisions.body: ● Yellow/Red Cards will initiate a review from the Judiciary Committee. They may issue reductions in League Score and potential other appropriate actions.

provisions.title: Tokens
provisions.body:
● Teams will receive 6 transfer tokens per season.
● Each token allows the team to add an “Active” competitor from another team or the “Free market” to their roster.
● A team can move one of their “Active” competitors to the “Free Agent Pool” at any time without cost in transfer tokens.
● Adding an “Active” competitor to the roster will cost you 1 token.

Competitors can register at any time, regardless of transfer windowActive vs Non-active (buhurt)

● Competitors who never joined a team are “Non-active” competitors
● Once a competitor is assigned to a team the competitor becomes “Active”
● Competitors don't lose the status “Active” after being dropped from a team, injuries or transfer window.

provisions.title: Transfer Window
provisions.body: Open transfer window from the 1st of December to the 14th of January. There will be no token reduced to readjust your teams during this time period

provisions.title: Country
provisions.body: A spatially clearly delimited area, in which its own administration with at least partial autonomy comes to bear, which emanates from an organization exercising power.

provisions.title: Region
provisions.body: A country/group of countries that choose to form a region together within a close geographical area.
Conference: Group of countries defined by Buhurt International in the above document.
Tournament: A competition held within the guidelines listed above.
Division: A set group of teams/competitors within a predetermined specification.
Category: A format of competitions established by the various rules of Buhurt International.

provisions.title: League: Organizational group for the purpose of competing beyond individual tournaments
provisions.body: by having ranking and standards.

provisions.title: League Score: Total points earned throughout a season to determine ranking throughout
provisions.body: sport.
Squad: 8 registered competitors on a team competing at an event.
